text:
sam: Quick check — I'm about to merge PR #4827 that splits modules/network into modules/vpc and modules/net-pol. I pinned provider versions in the root and added a generated providers.lock. Can someone confirm this won't break existing consumer stacks?

lina: Thanks for the ping. Two quick things: were the provider aliases preserved for the customer-connector module? Splitting can change provider inheritance.

sam: I added explicit provider mappings in modules/net-pol/versions.tf and modules/vpc/versions.tf, example: ```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "~> 5.0" }
  }
}

provider "aws" { alias = "org" region = var.region }
```
Should cover the aliasing use-cases.

matt: infra-bot reports a failing plan for staging after the split: ```
Error: Duplicate provider configuration
  on ../../modules/consumer/main.tf line 2, in provider "aws":
  2: provider "aws" {}
Found duplicate provider configuration with same alias.
```
This usually means a module and the root both define the same provider block without explicit alias mapping.

nisha: For secrets wiring — did you move any kms_key ARNs or secret references between modules? Consumer stacks expect secret manager ARNs at module outputs. If outputs moved, they'll break.

sam: Good catch. I kept outputs stable by adding compatibility outputs in the new vpc module: ```terraform
output "kms_arn" { value = aws_kms_key.main.arn }
# kept old name so dependent stacks don't need to change
```
I also updated the root module's providers.lock with `terraform providers lock` run on our standard backend.

infra-bot: plan check (staging) started by @sam. CI run id: ci-7891

matt: Re-ran local plan with terraform 1.6.7 and the generated lockfile and I get the same duplicate provider error unless I remove the provider {} block from the consumer stack that used to call the single-module variant. That suggests consumers need to explicitly pass provider = module.provider mapping now.

lina: Two options: 1) Add compatibility wrapper in modules/consumer that forwards root provider to the new nested modules using `providers = { aws = aws }` so consumers don't change. 2) Update all consumer stacks to pass `providers = { aws = module.vpc.aws }` but that will be a larger rollout. I'd prefer option 1 as a hotfix.

sam: I'll implement the compatibility wrapper in modules/consumer today and add a comment in CHANGELOG describing the provider pin and lockfile regeneration. Also will include upgrade notes: run `terraform init -upgrade` and reapply if you see provider mismatch.

nisha: Awesome. For secrets, can you ensure outputs are kept and add a short migration note for the security repo? I'll validate KMS permissions after you merge.

sam: Will do. I'll push a tiny PR to modules/consumer by EOD. If infra-bot approves CI, we can merge and then queue a canary deploy to staging. @deploy-bot can you schedule a canary once merged? :slightly_smiling_face:

deploy-bot: Received request to schedule canary. Will wait for merge event and smoke tests to pass.

lina: thanks — ping me after merge and I'll sweep dependent repos for any provider blocks that need explicit mapping. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks team — will update thread with PR link and CI status shortly.
